q: A distinctive feature of the working of the Public Accounts Committee is that:

options.A: Its reports are generally unanimous and no minutes of dissent are appended to them
options.B: Its reports are adopted by a majority vote of the members present
options.C: The Chairman of the Committee has a casting vote on all questions
options.D: Any member may record a minute of dissent in the report itself

q: An Audit Para included in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is treated as finally settled when:

options.A: The Ministry concerned furnishes its Action Taken Note
options.B: One year has elapsed from the laying of the Report before Parliament
options.C: The audit office drops the objection on its own
options.D: The Public Accounts Committee accepts the action taken by the Government on the para

q: In audit, the concept of 'materiality' refers to:

options.A: The total value of the stores held by the audited unit
options.B: The physical verification of the assets of the audited unit
options.C: The significance of an omission or misstatement of information, judged by whether it could influence the decisions of the users of the accounts
options.D: The minimum amount involved for which a separate audit paragraph is raised

q: Indian Government Accounting Standard (IGAS) 2, formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB), deals with:

options.B: Loans and Advances made by Governments
options.D: Disclosure of prior period items

q: The accounts of the Defence Services of the Union are compiled by:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Defence Accounts Department, headed by the Controller General of Defence Accounts

q: The detailed instructions and procedures governing the audit of the accounts of Indian Railways by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are contained in:

options.B: The Railway Audit Manual issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Indian Railway Finance Code

q: In order to watch the clearance of the objections raised by Audit in the Inspection Reports, the audited office maintains:

options.D: An Objection Book (Register), in which the objections and their settlement are recorded

q: Expenditure under a sub-head of a grant exceeds the provision under that sub-head, but the excess is offset by savings under other sub-heads and the total amount of the grant is not exceeded. In such a case:

options.A: An Excess Grant must be voted by Parliament to regularise the excess
options.B: No Excess Grant is required, as regularisation by Parliament is necessary only where the total amount of the grant or appropriation is exceeded
options.C: The FA&CAO can regularise the excess without reporting it anywhere
options.D: The excess under the sub-head is treated as unsanctioned expenditure

q: Re-appropriation of funds within a grant is NOT permissible:

options.A: From one sub-head to another sub-head of the same grant
options.B: To meet an anticipated excess under another head of the same grant, where savings are available
options.C: To meet expenditure on a 'new service' or 'new instrument of service' not contemplated in the Budget, without the prior approval of Parliament
options.D: Before the close of the financial year to which it relates

q: Interest paid on capital borrowed for the execution of a work, during the period of construction of that work, is ordinarily:

options.A: Charged to the revenue (working expenses) of the year in which it is paid
options.C: Adjusted against the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Capitalised, that is, charged to the Capital head of the work

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the classification of Government accounts, a Major Head represents a major function of the Government.
2. A Minor Head under a Major Head represents a programme undertaken to achieve the objectives of that function.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The cash balance held by the Government of India is accounted for as part of:

options.D: None of the three parts of the Government accounts

q: Under Article 283 of the Constitution, the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India and the Contingency Fund of India, the payment of moneys into and the withdrawal of moneys from them, and the custody of public moneys other than those credited to the Consolidated Fund, are regulated by:

options.A: Rules made by the Ministry of Finance
options.B: Resolutions of the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Law made by Parliament or, until such law is made, rules made by the President
options.D: Directions issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

q: Under Article 284 of the Constitution, all moneys received by, or deposited in the custody of, an officer of the Union or a court in connection with the affairs of the Union, other than revenues or public moneys credited to the Consolidated Fund, shall be:

options.A: Paid into the Public Account of India
options.B: Retained by the officer or court receiving them
options.C: Paid into the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Credited to the revenues of the Government

q: Which of the following does NOT form part of the Appropriation Accounts of a grant?

options.A: The grant-wise summary showing the final grant, the actual expenditure and the excess or saving
options.B: Explanations for the variations between the actual expenditure and the final grant
options.C: The certificate of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Profit and Loss Account of the Railway undertaking

q: Large and persistent savings under a grant, noticed year after year, are regarded in audit as indicative of:

options.A: Efficient financial management by the executive
options.B: Defective budgeting, that is, framing of estimates on the higher side without a proper assessment of the requirements
options.D: Prompt surrender of funds by the spending authorities

q: The 'escape clause' in the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) framework permits the Government to deviate from the fiscal deficit target, in exceptional circumstances such as national security, war or national calamity, up to:

options.D: 0.25 per cent of GDP

q: The FRBM Review Committee, which reviewed the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act in 2016 and recommended a debt-based fiscal framework, was chaired by:

options.D: Shaktikanta Das

q: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management framework, as amended following the recommendations of the FRBM Review Committee, prescribes for the Central Government a debt ceiling of:

options.D: 40 per cent of GDP

q: The assurance which a financial (attest) audit provides that the financial statements are free from material misstatement is:

options.A: Absolute assurance that no error or fraud exists
options.C: Reasonable assurance, which is a high level of assurance but not a guarantee
options.D: Assurance confined to the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts

q: The primary responsibility for the prevention and detection of fraud and error in an organisation rests with:

options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The management of the organisation

q: An Inspection Report issued by the audit office after local audit of a unit is ordinarily divided into:

options.A: Part I, containing serious irregularities requiring the attention of higher authorities, and Part II, containing other, less serious irregularities
options.B: Part I, containing the accounts of the unit, and Part II, containing the audit findings
options.C: Part I, meant for the Railway Board, and Part II, meant for the zonal Railway
options.D: It is not divided into parts at all

q: Where a loss of public money or stores occurs by reason of fraud, negligence or any other cause, the financial rules require that the loss should be reported promptly to:

options.B: The Accounts and Audit authorities and the next higher administrative authority
options.D: The Finance Commission

q: Under Article 292 of the Constitution, the executive power of the Union extends to borrowing upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India:

options.B: Only from the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Within such limits, if any, as may be fixed by Parliament by law
options.D: Only for financing railway projects

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 5,000 crore, ordinary working expenses of Rs 3,700 crore, appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of Rs 300 crore and appropriation to the Pension Fund of Rs 200 crore. Its Operating Ratio is:
A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 8,400 crore and working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 7,150 crore. Its net revenue is:

options.D: Rs 1,250 crore

q: The net revenue of a railway is Rs 900 crore and its capital-at-charge is Rs 12,000 crore. The return on capital-at-charge of the railway is:

Under the pre-merger financial convention, the dividend payable by a railway on a capital-at-charge (excluding the capital invested in strategic lines) of Rs 18,000 crore, at the rate of 4 per cent per annum, would amount to:

options.D: Rs 720 crore

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 7,500 crore, working expenses (including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund) of Rs 6,900 crore and dividend payable to General Finances of Rs 250 crore. Its surplus is:

options.D: Rs 350 crore

q: The reports of the Estimates Committee are presented to:

options.D: The Public Accounts Committee

q: Which of the following is a recognised feature of a sound system of internal control?

options.A: Rotation of duties among the staff from time to time, so that the same official does not continue indefinitely on the same work
options.B: Allowing one official to handle both the cash and the accounts of a transaction
options.C: Dispensing with independent verification of the work done
options.D: Checking of all transactions only at the end of the financial year

q: At the sittings of the Public Accounts Committee, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, or his representative:

options.A: Presides over the sittings of the Committee
options.B: Attends to assist the Committee with his expert advice on the audit paragraphs under examination
options.C: Presents the case of the Government on the audit paragraphs
options.D: Records the minutes of the Committee

q: Unlike the grants voted by Parliament, which lapse at the close of the financial year, the balances of the railway reserve funds, such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, held in the Public Account of India:

options.A: Also lapse at the close of the financial year
options.B: Are transferred to the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Do not lapse and are carried forward for utilisation in the following years
options.D: Are refunded to General Finances at the close of the year

q: The examination of the estimates by the Estimates Committee is:

options.A: Carried out only during the Budget session of Parliament
options.B: Carried out only once in five years
options.C: A continuous process, the Committee examining selected subjects and Ministries throughout the year and reporting to the Lok Sabha as it proceeds
options.D: Carried out after the accounts of the year have been closed

q: Under Article 280(3) of the Constitution, it is also the duty of the Finance Commission to make recommendations to the President as to:

options.A: The principles which should govern the grants-in-aid of the revenues of the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: The principles governing the classification of Government accounts
options.C: The rate of dividend payable by Railways to General Finances
options.D: The salaries and allowances of the Judges of the Supreme Court

q: The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India was enhanced by the Finance Act, 2020 from Rs 500 crore to:

options.D: Rs 50,000 crore

q: The Contingency Fund of India is in the nature of:

options.A: An imprest placed at the disposal of the President to enable advances to be made for meeting unforeseen expenditure, pending authorisation by Parliament
options.B: A deposit account forming part of the Public Account of India
options.C: A reserve fund built up out of the surplus revenues of the Government
options.D: A fund fed by market borrowings raised by the Government

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 268 of the Constitution, certain duties, such as stamp duties, are levied by the Union but are collected and appropriated by the States.
2. Under Article 270 of the Constitution, all taxes and duties in the Union List, other than those referred to in Articles 268 and 269 and any surcharge or cess, are shared between the Union and the States.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Under Article 293 of the Constitution, the executive power of a State extends to borrowing:

options.A: Only from the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: From foreign governments and international institutions directly
options.D: Within the territory of India upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of the State, within such limits as may be fixed by the Legislature of the State by law

q: Article 274 of the Constitution requires that a Bill which imposes or varies any tax or duty in which the States are interested shall not be introduced in either House of Parliament except:

options.A: On the recommendation of the President
options.B: With the concurrence of the Inter-State Council
options.C: With the approval of the Finance Commission
options.D: After consultation with all the State Governments

q: The levy and collection of Goods and Services Tax on supplies in the course of inter-State trade or commerce, and its apportionment between the Union and the States, are provided for in the Constitution under:

options.D: Article 271

q: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission, and the manner in which they are to be selected, are determined by:

options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Parliament, by law

q: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended that the share of the States in the net proceeds of the divisible pool of central taxes (vertical devolution) should be:

options.D: 45 per cent

q: For the purpose of distribution of taxes between the Union and the States, the expression 'net proceeds' of a tax or duty means:

options.A: The proceeds of the tax or duty reduced by the cost of collection
options.B: The gross collections of the tax or duty
options.C: The proceeds of the tax or duty after deducting refunds only
options.D: The proceeds of the tax or duty divided equally between the Union and the States

q: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 came into force in the year:
Under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management framework, the Central Government shall not give guarantees aggregating to an amount exceeding the following, in any financial year:

options.D: 5 per cent of GDP

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 lays down the fiscal responsibility targets for the Central Government.
2. The States have enacted their own Fiscal Responsibility Legislations prescribing deficit and debt targets for themselves.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Under the fiscal responsibility framework applicable to the States, the fiscal deficit of a State is targeted to be contained within:

options.A: 5 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product
options.C: 1 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product
options.D: 3 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product

q: The FRBM Review Committee of 2016 recommended an overall debt ceiling for the general Government (the Centre and the States together) of:

options.A: 60 per cent of GDP - 40 per cent for the Centre and 20 per cent for the States
options.D: 40 per cent of GDP for the Centre and the States together

q: The classification of Government expenditure into 'Plan' and 'Non-Plan' was discontinued in the Union Budget with effect from the Budget for:
Since the Budget for 2017-18, the Union Budget is presented to Parliament on:

options.A: The last working day of February

q: The proceeds realised by the Government from disinvestment of its shareholding in public sector undertakings are classified in the Union Budget as:

options.D: Public debt

q: In the accounts and Budget documents of the Government of India, the collections under the small savings schemes and the balances of Provident Funds are shown as:

options.A: 'Other liabilities' of the Government, distinct from its public debt

options.D: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India

options.D: Rs 12,00,000 crore

options.D: Rs 6,40,000 crore

options.B: Loans and advances made by Governments

options.D: Guarantees given by Governments - disclosure requirements

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Government Accounting Standards (IGAS) issued so far are based on the cash basis of accounting followed in Government accounts.

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: While examining the accounts of the Government, the Public Accounts Committee is also required to satisfy itself that:

options.D: Representatives of the administrative Ministries only

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 5,000 crore, ordinary working expenses of Rs 3,900 crore, appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of Rs 250 crore and appropriation to the Pension Fund of Rs 250 crore. Its Operating Ratio is:

options.D: Rs 100 crore

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Under Article 293(3) of the Constitution, a State may not, without the consent of the Government of India, raise any loan if:
